summary: Josephine County, OR 30-foot fire lookout tower on Mount Reuben, built 1931-32, replaced in 1950 and removed or destroyed in 1967; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot tower with a 14-by-14-foot cab (register: built 1932), with an R-1 style cab per the 1931 Forest Lookouts item; replaced by a 30-foot treated timber tower
facts.status_note: Replacement tower removed or destroyed in 1967; no source describes remains at the summit

staffing.status: Dick Bland of Merlin named lookout in 1931; the 1940 plan has the point manned from very early June to late September

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (station begun by the Siskiyou National Forest in 1931)

events.note: 30-foot tower with an R-1 style cab constructed (Forest Lookouts); the register dates the 14-by-14-foot cab tower to 1932
Dick Bland of Merlin named lookout for the new station
1940 plan: point manned very early in June in two of three years and kept staffed until late September in all three years
Replaced by a 30-foot treated timber tower; register and firelookout.com say 1950, Forest Lookouts says 1951 new lookout constructed
Building maintenance noted in the Southwest Oregon District Annual Report (painted interior); 1962 maintenance also recorded
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered March 28, 2011 as US 897, OR 264; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the 30-foot tower with a 14-by-14-foot cab to 1932. The Forest Lookouts history says a 30-foot tower with an R-1 style cab was constructed in 1931, and that the station was established by January 1932. The story gives both dates.
The register and firelookout.com date the 30-foot treated timber replacement to 1950; the Forest Lookouts history gives 1951.
The register says removed in 1967; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967. The sources do not describe how it ended.
The register lists the Oregon Department of Forestry; the Forest Lookouts history says the 1931 station was begun by the Siskiyou National Forest. The sources do not say when administration changed.

notes_for_editor: Records agree on a 30-foot tower and on removal or destruction in 1967, but disagree on the 1931 and 1932 build dates and on the 1950 and 1951 replacement. No source describes remains or public access today, so no access key is recorded.
